title: The Wanting Chemical
question: Dopamine is called the pleasure chemical — yet Berridge's rats, dopamine-depleted, still show liking faces for sugar while refusing to work for it. What does dopamine actually drive?
correctExplanation: Wanting and pursuit — dopamine energizes seeking; liking lives elsewhere (opioid hotspots). Depleted rats enjoy but won't strive.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is wanting and pursuit. Pleasure, faces, and buds miss it: liking faces survive dopamine loss while lever-pressing dies. Motivation, not hedonia, is dopamine's business.
lessonContent:
Motivation differs from hedonia chemically.
Seeking runs on separate fuel from savoring.
Depleted strivers still smile at sugar.
Wanting circuits drive pursuit daily.

title: The Liking Spot
question: If dopamine isn't pleasure, what mediates actual enjoyment — the hedonic gloss on sweet tastes?
correctExplanation: Hedonic hotspots using opioids — cubic-millimeter zones where pleasure is generated. Dopamine wants; opioids like.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is hedonic hotspots using opioids. Adrenaline, acid, and ears miss it: pleasure lives in tiny opioid-sensitive patches. Separate chemistry, separate feeling.
lessonContent:
Pleasure lives in millimeter patches.
Opioids gloss what dopamine pursues.
Separate chemistries, separate feelings.
Wanting chases; liking savors.

title: The Bitter Paradox
question: Long-term addicts report enjoying drugs less and less while craving them more and more. What splits in opposite directions?
correctExplanation: Wanting versus liking — incentive sensitization: wanting sensitizes upward while liking tolerates downward. Craving grows as joy shrinks.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is wanting versus liking. Vitals, shoes, and height miss it: sensitized pursuit plus blunted pleasure defines addiction's cruelty. More craved, less enjoyed — simultaneously.
lessonContent:
Craving grows while joy shrinks.
Sensitization splits pursuit from pleasure.
Addiction's cruelty is directional split.
More wanted, less liked: the trap.

title: The Frozen Will
question: Parkinson's depletes dopamine, freezing movement and motivation — yet patients can still feel pleasure when it arrives. What does dopamine loss primarily steal?
correctExplanation: The drive to act — akinesia and apathy, not anhedonia, define dopamine loss. Movement and motivation share fuel.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the drive to act. Smiles, colors, and memories miss it: patients feel arriving pleasures but cannot initiate pursuit. Starting, not savoring, needs dopamine.
lessonContent:
Starting needs dopamine; savoring less so.
Initiation fails while enjoyment persists.
Movement shares fuel with motivation.
Drive, not delight, depletes first.

title: The Dulled Patient
question: Antipsychotics block dopamine — calming psychosis but often flattening motivation into avolition. What price does blockade exact?
correctExplanation: Initiative and drive — D2 blockade quiets hallucinations and ambitions together. Calibration, not elimination, is the art.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is initiative and drive. Nails, hair, and shoes miss it: damping salience damps all pursuits, delusional and legitimate alike. Doses balance psychosis against purpose.
lessonContent:
Damping salience damps all pursuits.
Doses balance psychosis against purpose.
Calibration beats elimination in prescribing.
Quiet minds need kept purposes.

title: The Endless Scroll
question: Feeds deliver unpredictable social rewards on variable schedules — the same schedule that addicts gamblers. What design feature hooks users?
correctExplanation: Variable-ratio delivery — unpredictable pellets sustain checking longest: slots, feeds, identical schedules. Predictability would free users.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is variable-ratio reward delivery. Fonts, speeds, and colors miss it: schedule shapes behavior, not surface. Unpredictable rewards farm wanting relentlessly.
lessonContent:
Schedules shape behavior, never surfaces.
Unpredictable pellets sustain checking longest.
Slots and feeds share blueprints.
Predictability would free all users.

title: The Heart Button
question: Users insist they dislike an app yet tap its notification heart a hundred times daily. What do the taps measure?
correctExplanation: Conditioned wanting — cues trigger pursuit circuits regardless of enjoyment. Taps count craving, never contentment.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is conditioned wanting, not liking. Satisfaction, fitness, and brightness miss it: red badges hijack seeking while users report dislike. Behavior reveals wanting; surveys reveal liking.
lessonContent:

Taps count craving, never contentment.

title: The Surprise Signal
question: Schultz's monkeys: dopamine neurons fired at unexpected juice — then, once learned, at the predicting cue instead, going quiet at delivery. What does dopamine report?
correctExplanation: Reward-prediction error — surprise, not sweetness: unexpected good news fires, expected delivery flatlines. Dopamine is news, not dessert.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is reward-prediction error. Sweetness, thirst, and temperature miss it: neurons track better-or-worse-than-expected precisely. Predicted juice earns silence; surprising cues earn bursts.
lessonContent:
News, never dessert, fires neurons.
Surprise drives what sweetness cannot.
Expected delivery earns silence fully.
Prediction errors teach everything.

title: The Predicted Juice
question: Once monkeys fully learn that a cue means juice, dopamine response at actual delivery drops to baseline. Why the silence?
correctExplanation: No surprise remains — fully predicted rewards carry zero prediction error. Silence is accurate forecasting, not fatigue.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no surprise remains. Fatigue, bitterness, and sleep miss it: neurons signal deviations, and perfect prediction deviates nothing. Quiet delivery means learned world.
lessonContent:
Perfect prediction deviates nothing.
Silence means learned worlds fully.
Deviations, not deliveries, drive firing.
Quiet juice proves accurate models.

title: The Near Miss
question: Slot machines display near-misses (two cherries plus one lemon) that lose money yet sustain play fiercely. What do near-misses fuel?
correctExplanation: Wanting without paying — near-misses trigger prediction-error circuitry like partial wins. Losses disguised as almosts sustain pursuit.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is wanting without paying. Accounts, bills, and budgets miss it: almost-winning fires wanting circuits while paying nothing. Designers engineer hope from defeat.
lessonContent:

Losses disguised sustain pursuit fiercely.
Hope engineered from defeat pays casinos.

title: The Loot Chest
question: Gacha games sell random-chance chests whose contents thrill at reveal, whatever the contents. What makes opening compulsive?
correctExplanation: Variable rewards plus prediction error — random loot with fanfare maximizes wanting circuitry. Contents matter less than ceremony.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is variable rewards plus prediction error. Graphics, sounds, and keepers miss it: uncertainty plus reveal-ceremony drives compulsion. Dopamine prices the opening, not the prize.

title: The Novelty Bonus
question: Familiar partners, familiar foods, familiar routes fade in appeal — while novelty rekindles pursuit (the Coolidge effect). What renews wanting?
correctExplanation: Mere novelty — newness alone re-fires wanting circuits regardless of quality. Coolidge bulls and bored shoppers share wiring.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is mere novelty itself. Nutrition, bonds, and prices miss it: newness per se triggers pursuit machinery. Familiarity starves what novelty feeds automatically.
lessonContent:

title: The Split Tolerance
question: With repeated drug use, pleasure fades (tolerance) while craving grows (sensitization). What moves in opposite directions?
correctExplanation: Liking down, wanting up — tolerance blunts enjoyment while sensitization sharpens pursuit. Opposite arrows define addiction's trap.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is liking down, wanting up. Weight, hearts, and shoes miss it: two adaptations diverge — hedonic systems habituate, incentive systems sensitize. Enjoy less, chase more: the spiral.
lessonContent:
Adaptations diverge cruelly in addiction.
Habituation dulls; sensitization sharpens.
Enjoy-less-chase-more is the spiral.
Opposite arrows trap users fully.

title: The Weekend Reset

correctExplanation: Receptor dynamics — sensitivity remodels over weeks via expression and circuitry, never weekends. Biology ignores retreat schedules.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is receptor dynamics. Willpower, batteries, and stars miss it: turnover and remodeling run on biological timescales. Weekends rest minds; they don't rebuild receptors.
lessonContent:

title: The Calming Stimulant

correctExplanation: Boosted dopamine signaling — raising signal-to-noise steadies control circuits: paradox resolved. Brains need tuning, not just fuel.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is boosted dopamine signaling. Sugar, temperature, and bedtimes miss it: underpowered control circuits overfire chaotically; support steadies them. Stimulation calms through better brakes.

title: The Morning Blocker
question: Caffeine sharpens mornings without touching dopamine transporters directly. What receptor does it block?
correctExplanation: Adenosine receptors — blocking sleep-signal reception masks fatigue; dopamine rises only downstream. Coffee mutes tiredness, never manufactures energy.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is adenosine receptors. Transporters, pumps, and factories miss it: caffeine antagonizes fatigue signals upstream. Masked tiredness differs from true vigor.
lessonContent:

Upstream blocks mute sleep signals.
Downstream effects follow indirectly.

title: The Sweet Equivalence

incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is scale differences. Calories, taste, and nature miss it: mechanisms rhyme while magnitudes differ astronomically. Headlines equate; dose-response distinguishes.
lessonContent:
